chunks: Muhammad ibn Sinan narrated from Yusuf ibn 'Imran, from Ya'qub ibn Shu'ayb, who said, 'I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say:'

Verily, Allah revealed to Adam (peace be upon him): 'I have gathered for you all speech in four statements.' He asked, 'What are they, O Lord?' He said, 'One is for Me, one is for you, one is between Me and you, and one is between you and the people.' He said, 'O Lord, explain them to me so that I may act upon them.' He said, 'As for that which is for Me, it is that you worship Me and do not associate anything with Me. As for that which is for you, I will recompense you for your action when you are most in need of it. As for that which is between Me and you, it is upon you to supplicate and upon Me to answer. As for that which is between you and the people, it is that you should be pleased for the people what you are pleased for yourself.'
ai.seo_question: What are the four fundamental principles of worship and social conduct revealed to Adam?
ai.summary: In *Kitab al-Zuhd*, this hadith presents a concise theological framework where divine revelation to Adam (AS) distills complex jurisprudence into four relational pillars: vertical worship (*li-llah*), individual recompense (*laka*), the dynamic of supplication and response (*bayna-na*), and social ethics (*bayna-ka wa-bayna-an-nas*). Shia scholars often cite this to demonstrate the holistic nature of *Tawhid*, linking monotheism directly to social justice and the reciprocity of divine mercy through *Dua*.
